## Motivation

To improve sglang out-of-box experience on AWS GPU clusters.

## Modifications
1. Added a new build target: `runtime-efa` to build image with EFA user space libraries and `mooncake-transfer-engine-efa`
2. Extended CI workflow scripts to build and publish the newly added target images.

NOTE: 
The PR adds a new target `runtime-efa` instead of updating the existing `runtime` because the `rdma-core` version from EFA installer is different from the version comes with distro. Though the latest `rdma-core` version from the EFA installer should work for non-EFA platforms as well, we didn't test that configuration. And also not to interfere with the existing build configurations, we took a new target approach.

Worth fixing in this stage (item 2 turned out to be already fixed on main):

1. **NCCL doesn't pick up aws-ofi-nccl by default.** The installer puts `libnccl-ofi-ngc-v3` in `/opt/amazon/ofi-nccl/lib`, which ships only `libnccl-net-ofi.so`/`libnccl-tuner-ofi.so` and no `libnccl-net.so`. NCCL therefore logs `NET/Plugin: Could not find: libnccl-net.so` and falls back to sockets.
   - default: `Using network Socket`, busbw **18.8 GB/s**
   - `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi`: `NET/OFI Initializing aws-ofi-nccl 1.21.1`, `Using network Libfabric`, busbw **404 GB/s**

   Suggest adding `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi` to the stage's `ENV`.

2. ~~**The `runtime` base has no gdrcopy.**~~ *(edited: already fixed on main)* The published `lmsysorg/sglang:latest-runtime` (built 9/18) is missing `libgdrapi` (`ldd /usr/bin/gdrcopy_sanity` reports `libgdrapi.so.2 => not found`), so libfabric logs `gdrcopy_dl_hmem_init failed!` there. The cause was the runtime stage's COPY source `/usr/lib/libgdrapi.so*`, which main already fixed in #37442 (e047e50d4e, 9/24). After rebasing, `runtime-efa` inherits the fix, so no change is needed in this PR.

Minor: the runtime image has no `torchrun` on `PATH`, so use `python3 -m torch.distributed.run`.

The arm64 image also gets published under the `-runtime-efa` tags, since `_docker-build-and-publish.yml` builds both arches. But Mooncake's `rdma` transport needs RC verbs and EFA only does SRD, so on Grace-based EFA instances Mooncake won't actually work over EFA with this image.

Was arm64 tested at all? If not, maybe skip arm64 for this target for now, or document that arm64 only gets libfabric.

Suggest adding `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi` here. While at it, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` can go, per @erezzarum's comment above: the installer's `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/000_efa.conf` already puts `/opt/amazon/efa/lib` first. I verified that the AWS libfabric is still the one loaded without this ENV.

```suggestion
ENV PATH="/opt/amazon/efa/bin:${PATH}" \
    NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi
```

Why `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN`: the installer puts `libnccl-ofi-ngc-v3` in `/opt/amazon/ofi-nccl/lib`. That package ships only `libnccl-net-ofi.so`/`libnccl-tuner-ofi.so`, with no `libnccl-net.so`, so NCCL's default plugin lookup misses it and falls back to sockets. On 2x p5en.48xlarge, 2x8 GPUs, 512 MiB all_reduce:
- default: `NET/Plugin: Could not find: libnccl-net.so`, `Using network Socket`, busbw 18.8 GB/s
- `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi`: `NET/OFI Initializing aws-ofi-nccl 1.21.1`, `Using network Libfabric`, busbw 404 GB/s

Adding some Mooncake-side context (I maintain Mooncake's EFA transport). It's actually a bit worse than "won't work over EFA": in the standard wheel, `rdma` auto-discovery also picks up the EFA NICs as verbs devices. The RC QP creation then fails (`Failed to create QP: Operation not supported`) and the transfer hangs instead of falling back. I reproduced this on p5en with the standard wheel. kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4355 makes RDMA skip EFA NICs and fall back to TCP, but it isn't released yet.

On arm64 specifically:
- aarch64 builds of `mooncake-transfer-engine-efa*` are merged (kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4305) and will first ship in Mooncake v0.3.14. After that, the amd64-only condition on the wheel swap can be dropped, and arm64 can use `MOONCAKE_PROTOCOL=efa` too.
- Until then, for arm64 in this target, I'd either skip arm64 or set `MOONCAKE_PROTOCOL=tcp` there and document it, rather than `rdma`.
- The rest of the stage (EFA installer, NIXL LIBFABRIC, aws-ofi-nccl) supports aarch64. I've only validated EFA on Graviton (CPU/DRAM), not on Grace/GB200.

 #   - lmsysorg/sglang:v{version}-runtime, lmsysorg/sglang:latest-runtime
 #   - lmsysorg/sglang:v{version}-cu130-runtime, lmsysorg/sglang:latest-cu130-runtime
 #
+# Plus the AWS EFA variant of the same runtime (adds the EFA userspace stack and,
+# on amd64, the EFA build of the Mooncake wheel):
+#   - lmsysorg/sglang:v{version}-runtime-efa, lmsysorg/sglang:latest-runtime-efa
+#   - lmsysorg/sglang:v{version}-cu130-runtime-efa, lmsysorg/sglang:latest-cu130-runtime-efa

@@ -52,3 +57,27 @@ jobs:
           {"cuda": "cu130", "tags": ["v${{ needs.resolve-version.outputs.version }}-runtime", "latest-runtime", "v${{ needs.resolve-version.outputs.version }}-cu130-runtime", "latest-cu130-runtime"]}
         ]
     secrets: inherit
+
+  # Deliberately serialized behind `build-and-publish` rather than run in
+  # parallel: both calls land on the same named self-hosted runners
+  # (x64-docker-build-node / arm-docker-build-node), where each job does
+  # `sudo rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"/*` and `docker system prune -af` and writes
+  # a fixed /tmp/docker-metadata-cu130.args. Concurrent calls would clobber each
+  # other's workspace and metadata.
+  #
+  # Note this is a full second image build, not an incremental one: the reusable
+  # workflow passes --no-cache, so no layers are shared with the job above even
+  # though `runtime-efa` only adds two layers on top of `runtime`.
+  build-and-publish-efa:
+    needs: [resolve-version, build-and-publish]
+    uses: ./.github/workflows/_docker-build-and-publish.yml
+    with:
+      docker_target: runtime-efa
+      sgl_version: ${{ needs.resolve-version.outputs.version }}
+      use_environment: prod
+      image_repo: ${{ inputs.image_repo || 'lmsysorg/sglang' }}
+      tag_config: |

@@ -808,3 +808,124 @@ LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang" \
 
 # Default command
 CMD ["/bin/bash"]
+
+# =============================================================================
+# AWS EFA runtime (opt-in target)
+# =============================================================================
+# Extends `runtime` with the pieces needed to drive AWS EFA from inside the
+# container, so no host-side EFA installation is required:
+#
+#   1. The AWS EFA userspace stack (libfabric plus its EFA provider).
+#   2. The EFA build of the Mooncake transfer engine wheel.
+#
+#   docker build --target runtime-efa -t sglang:efa      -f docker/Dockerfile .
+#
+# NOTE: this stage is last, so it is what a bare `docker build` with no
+# --target produces. Always pass --target explicitly.
+#
+# Kernel modules and host limits remain the responsibility of the container
+# host.
+FROM runtime AS runtime-efa
+
+ARG TARGETARCH
+ARG EFA_INSTALLER_VERSION=1.50.0
+ARG EFA_INSTALLER_SHA256=fa6dff8593d866866c13cb4640d9059835cd4efa427971f100ab40c97bef2841
+
+# Install the AWS EFA userspace stack.
+#
+# `set -eux` is required: the body is a `;`-separated sequence run by /bin/sh,
+# so without it only the last command decides the RUN exit status and a failed
+# install would silently produce an empty layer.
+#
+# The distro libfabric1 stays installed on purpose -- libopenmpi3t64 depends on
+# it, so removing it would break that package. Both libfabric.so.1 copies
+# coexist; the ENV below makes the AWS one win deterministically.
+RUN set -eux; \
+    EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE="/tmp/aws-efa-installer-${EFA_INSTALLER_VERSION}.tar.gz"; \
+    curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-all-errors \
+        "https://efa-installer.amazonaws.com/aws-efa-installer-${EFA_INSTALLER_VERSION}.tar.gz" \
+        -o "${EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE}"; \
+    echo "${EFA_INSTALLER_SHA256}  ${EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE}" | sha256sum -c -; \
+    tar -xzf "${EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE}" -C /tmp; \
+    # efa_installer.sh apt-installs pciutils/environment-modules/tcl, and the
+    # runtime stage purges /var/lib/apt/lists, so refresh the lists first.
+    apt-get update -y; \
+    # --minimal is not usable here: it installs rdma-core but skips libfabric,
+    # which is the only piece needed for the EFA data path.
+    (cd /tmp/aws-efa-installer && \
+        ./efa_installer.sh -y --skip-kmod --skip-limit-conf --no-verify); \
+    test -x /opt/amazon/efa/bin/fi_info; \
+    /opt/amazon/efa/bin/fi_info --version; \
+    # Assert the EFA provider is actually compiled into this libfabric. `-l`
+    # lists providers without needing EFA hardware, so it works during a build.
+    /opt/amazon/efa/bin/fi_info -l | grep -q '^efa:'; \
+    # Assert the AWS libfabric precedes the distro 1.17.0 in the loader cache.
+    # Match the first libfabric.so.1 entry, since `ldconfig -p` prints
+    # "libfabric.so.1 (libc6,x86-64) => /path" and order decides the winner.
+    ldconfig -p | grep -m1 'libfabric\.so\.1' | grep -q '/opt/amazon/efa/lib/'; \
+    rm -rf "${EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE}" /tmp/aws-efa-installer \
+        /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+# Prefer the AWS libfabric over the distro libfabric1 that libopenmpi3t64 pulls
+# in, and expose fi_info/fi_pingpong for debugging EFA from inside the image.
+ENV PATH="/opt/amazon/efa/bin:${PATH}" \
+    NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi
+# Swap the standard Mooncake wheel for the EFA build. Both wheels install the
+# same `mooncake` module, so the standard one must be removed first rather than
+# installed over. --no-deps preserves the dependency stack the image was built
+# against, matching docs/advanced_features/pd_disaggregation.mdx.
+#
+# The EFA wheel is published for x86_64 only (manylinux_2_35_x86_64), so on other
+# architectures this step is skipped and the standard wheel is kept.
+#
+# The EFA wheel is pinned to the version of the standard wheel already in the
+# image, read from its distribution metadata before it is removed, so the two
+# can never drift apart. Versions are read from metadata rather than by
+# importing the module: the extension links libcuda.so.1, absent from a
+# GPU-less builder.
+RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip \
+    set -eux; \
+    if [ "${TARGETARCH}" = "amd64" ]; then \
+        pkg_version() { python3 -c 'import importlib.metadata as m, sys; print(m.version(sys.argv[1]))' "$1"; }; \
+        MOONCAKE_VERSION="$(pkg_version mooncake-transfer-engine-cuda13)"; \
+        test -n "${MOONCAKE_VERSION}"; \
+        python3 -m pip uninstall -y mooncake-transfer-engine-cuda13; \
+        python3 -m pip install --no-deps \
+            "mooncake-transfer-engine-efa-cuda13==${MOONCAKE_VERSION}"; \
+        test "$(pkg_version mooncake-transfer-engine-efa-cuda13)" = "${MOONCAKE_VERSION}"; \
+        # `! cmd` is exempt from `set -e`, so a leftover standard wheel would not
+        # fail the build that way; check for it explicitly instead.
+        if pkg_version mooncake-transfer-engine-cuda13 >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
+            echo "mooncake-transfer-engine-cuda13 is still installed" >&2; \
+            exit 1; \
+        fi; \
+    else \
+        echo "TARGETARCH=${TARGETARCH}: mooncake-transfer-engine-efa-cuda13 is \
+x86_64-only, keeping the standard wheel (Mooncake EFA protocol unavailable)"; \
+    fi
+
+# Mooncake protocol, derived from the architecture. amd64 carries the EFA wheel
+# so it can use the `efa` protocol; other architectures kept the standard wheel,
+# which speaks `rdma` over the AWS rdma-core installed above. Setting `efa` there
+# would name a protocol the installed wheel does not implement.
+#
+# ENV cannot be made conditional and cannot read anything a RUN produced, so the
+# value is derived with ARG substitution. `#amd64` strips that exact prefix, so
+# ARCH_IF_NOT_AMD64 is empty on amd64 and holds the architecture name everywhere
+# else; `:+` maps that to rdma, and `:-` supplies efa for the empty case. The
+# ENV line reads as: rdma if not amd64, otherwise efa.
+#
+# The test is deliberately "not amd64" rather than "is amd64" so it matches the
+# `[ "${TARGETARCH}" = "amd64" ]` test used by the Mooncake swap above, keeping a
+# third architecture on rdma alongside the standard wheel. Writing it positively
+# would require stripping `arm64`, which actually means "not arm64" and would
+# wrongly select efa on any future architecture.
+#
+# Nested expansion (${PROTO_${TARGETARCH}}) is not an option -- BuildKit rejects
+# it with "unsupported modifier ($) in substitution" -- and concatenating two
+# complementary `:+` expansions silently yields "rdmaefa" on a third
+# architecture, so keep the explicit `:+` then `:-` pair.
+ARG ARCH_IF_NOT_AMD64=${TARGETARCH#amd64}
+ARG PROTOCOL_IF_NOT_AMD64=${ARCH_IF_NOT_AMD64:+tcp}
+ENV MOONCAKE_PROTOCOL=${PROTOCOL_IF_NOT_AMD64:-efa} \
+    SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND=LIBFABRIC


Why `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN`: the installer puts `libnccl-ofi-ngc-v3` in `/opt/amazon/ofi-nccl/lib`. That package ships only `libnccl-net-ofi.so`/`libnccl-tuner-ofi.so`, with no `libnccl-net.so`, so NCCL's default plugin lookup misses it and falls back to sockets. On 2x p5en.48xlarge, 2x8 GPUs, 512 MiB all_reduce:
- default: `NET/Plugin: Could not find: libnccl-net.so`, `Using network Socket`, busbw 18.8 GB/s
- `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi`: `NET/OFI Initializing aws-ofi-nccl 1.21.1`, `Using network Libfabric`, busbw 404 GB/s

Adding some Mooncake-side context (I maintain Mooncake's EFA transport). It's actually a bit worse than "won't work over EFA": in the standard wheel, `rdma` auto-discovery also picks up the EFA NICs as verbs devices. The RC QP creation then fails (`Failed to create QP: Operation not supported`) and the transfer hangs instead of falling back. I reproduced this on p5en with the standard wheel. kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4355 makes RDMA skip EFA NICs and fall back to TCP, but it isn't released yet.

On arm64 specifically:
- aarch64 builds of `mooncake-transfer-engine-efa*` are merged (kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4305) and will first ship in Mooncake v0.3.14. After that, the amd64-only condition on the wheel swap can be dropped, and arm64 can use `MOONCAKE_PROTOCOL=efa` too.
- Until then, for arm64 in this target, I'd either skip arm64 or set `MOONCAKE_PROTOCOL=tcp` there and document it, rather than `rdma`.
- The rest of the stage (EFA installer, NIXL LIBFABRIC, aws-ofi-nccl) supports aarch64. I've only validated EFA on Graviton (CPU/DRAM), not on Grace/GB200.
